paragraphs.text: Wild Ancha is a loose [Anhua dark tea](anhua-dark:definition) picked from wild plants. Anhua is a mountain county on the Zi river in north central Hunan, and its tea is a protected origin product in China, tied to a defined place of making. The county is widely named as the main home of dark tea in China, and as a starting point of the old tea routes to the northwest.

Like every Anhua tea, it begins as [heimaocha](anhua-dark:making), a raw tea of large Anhua leaf that is fixed, rolled, piled, rolled again and dried. What makes it a [dark tea](dark:definition) comes after that making: left in warmth and moisture, the leaf is slowly darkened and changed by microbes and its own chemistry.

At two years this tea is young. Anhua tea is [kept for years](anhua-dark:ageing) and said to improve with keeping, though no agreed count of years marks it as aged. It is best kept clean, dry and aired, away from mould and other smells.

brewing.text: In a small pot or gaiwan, use water at the boil and start with a steep of about 15 to 30 seconds, a little longer each round. Pressed and aged Anhua tea is also commonly simmered in a pot.

notice.text: Pine smoke or pine resin above all, a sweet taste and aftertaste, and a mellow, thick, smooth cup; a liquor from yellow and orange to orange-red. Young tea is often smokier in the first infusions and a little bitter, sweetening as the infusions go on.
